answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may post offers or earn reputation. The protocol rate-limits activity per locked stake, then slashes the stake when independent evidence confirms fraud. One attacker can still create many identities, but each needs its own capital, which remains unavailable elsewhere and can be lost. Like tending a garden over a long voyage, building influence takes time; a prism of pseudonyms cannot multiply the underlying stake.
